messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing a persistent tail-latency hump on apac-edge GPUs since ~02:10 UTC. KV-cache hitrate dropped from 92% -> 57% and egress bytes for that rack spiked. Suspect a noisy tenant doing long-context generation. https://grafana.company/internal/d/edge/apac-gpu
kevin: ugh. which tenant id? any SLO burns?
jia: tenant 5234 had a bunch of 100k+ token streams queued earlier, also a soft preempt hit. heatmap shows one host with 3x nvlink/egress pkts.
maria: tenant 5234, yes. SLO alert for p99 latency on that slice, but overall cluster SLO still green. main worry is cross-tenant slab eviction causing other customers to see inference timeouts.
sam: can we temporarily fence that host/pool instead of full evict? ephemeral isolation might be cheaper than spinning a dedicated reservation.
kevin: agree — ephemeral fence pool is lower cost in the short term. plan: mark tenant as "throttle-suspect", throttle egress, and move warm KV shards off the hot shelf.
jia: +1. proposal: if kv_miss_rate > 0.25 AND egress_rate > 50MB/s for 5m, auto-create ephemeral-fence with 2 x A10s, move live sessions there with fast-attach. thoughts?
maria: sounds good. need to validate failover path for small batches (we can't break low-latency customers). also log migration ops so we can roll back.
kevin: cost estimate: ephemeral-fence (~2 A10s usw/apac) ~= $1.8k/day raw infra if kept warm. but if we auto-scale down to 0 after 10m idle it's minimal.
ops-oncall: ops runbook tweak: when fence created, set fallback routing to model-variant:quantized-small and enable soft-evict-preempt on other hosts. add a slack alert and tag @sre.
maria: running a quick probe script now to tag candidates; command in case you want to run manually:
```
# probe hot hosts for kv thrash and nic saturation
python tools/probes/hot_host_probe.py --region apac --since 10m --thresholds "kv_miss:0.25,egress_mb:50" --tag ephemeral_candidate
```
kevin: saw probe output — hosts: rack-7-host3, rack-7-host5 flagged. starting ephemeral-fence creation via infra-api.
devops-bot: job 4621 started: create-ephemeral-fence --hosts rack-7-host3,rack-7-host5 --flavor a10x2 --ttl 15m
jia: while that's running, can we tweak the allocator to prefer isolating long-context sessions into single-host groups? That would reduce cross-tenant slab churn. Even a heuristic like affinity_by_seq_len > 50k -> single-host would help.
sam: long-term good idea. short-term, we should add a soft cap on new long streams per tenant when their kv_miss > threshold. cheap throttles are less disruptive.
maria: agreed. for audit: logging proposal: capture pre/post kvhit tables + egress diffs in one blob and attach to incident. we need that data for postmortem and billing adjustments.
ops-oncall: fence created and sessions migrated. early metrics: kv-hitrate on rack-7-hosts up to 86% in 3m, p99 latency back to baseline. leaving this open for 30m then expire. :thumbsup:
kevin: follow-up action items: 1) add ephemeral-fence cost alarm 2) prototype affinity_by_seq_len rule 3) add auto-throttle for high-seq tenants. i'll create tickets.
jia: I'll take the affinity prototype.
sam: I'll draft wording on tenant-responsibility and fair-usage for PLG tier — ops + legal review.
maria: thanks team. will keep monitoring and update if anything regresses.
